newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end marginally firmer on moderate volume.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end marginally firmer on moderate volume.

text.p: * New Zealand shares end firmer as FCL Paper, Carter gain
* No surprises from BIL with NZ$116 million half yr profit
* Telecom has investors betwixt and between
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
327 +5 * NZSC cap index +1.60 at 5,125.13
363 +5 * Volume NZ$51.2 million. Futures at 1,136
668 nil * Other movers - -8 +10
New Zealand shares closed marginally firmer on Thursday, led higher towards the close by forestry stocks Fletcher Paper and Carter Holt Harvey .
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 4.92 points stronger at 2,288.18, with FCL Paper up six at NZ$2.93 and Carter Holt up five to $3.27.

"Fletcher Paper seems to be one of the favoured stocks as a consensus among leading brokers, so it's not surprising to see quite a bit of buying there," said Merrill Lynch broker Matt Cunneen, who added that Carter appeared to bouncing back a touch
from recent pressure.
All leading stocks made modest gains on the day with the exception of Telecom, which closed flat at $6.68.

After earnings concerns saw Telecom plunge from $7.55 in mid-January to $6.45 at the end of February, the market leader has been struggling in the $6.60s. Cunneen said investors were presently betwixt and between when it came to Telecom.

"There's a dichotomy of views in that stock. Some people are certain that we've seen the bottom, but others are a bit more cautious and are saying the circumstances that forced the stock down are still there.
"So there's a tendency for a lot of investors to remain underweight in it even though it's come back," he said.
Brierley Investments Ltd ended one cent firmer at $1.37 despite reporting a half year profit of $116 million, down from $170 million a year ago.
Brokers said the result was expected as BIL had not made any large asset sales to boost its profit.
"People really look at the values of the underlying assets, and those have improved so consequently we've seen the stock reasonably well supported," Cunneen said.

The market was not so kind to Wrightson. The rural services group ended eight cent weaker at $0.96 after reporting a first half profit of $1.25 million, down from $5.74 million, and revising its full year result forecasts sharply down.
